framework: Scoring settings for models M1-M3 (GDD section 12)

m1_interests.model: One joint model: Thurstonian IRT for forced choices and the planner ranking block + graded response model for reaction taps (3 categories), all loading on the same six traits
m1_interests.identification: trait means 0 and variances 1 in the calibration sample; GRM thresholds give the absolute anchor
m1_interests.planner: one ranking block (3 picked of 6); its 9 binary outcomes share option utilities, so they are not treated as independent
m1_interests.estimator: MAP with an N(0, Sigma) prior; SE = posterior SD from the Laplace approximation. No full quadrature grid (41^6 points would be infeasible); quasi-Monte-Carlo EAP with 2,000 Sobol points is used only as a check in the simulation study
m1_interests.adaptive: next scenes maximise expected information for the type with the largest SE, within pairs.json coverage and exposure caps
m1_interests.pre_calibration: Open-Source Psychometrics RIASEC dataset via simulated game choices (feasibility only; parameters marked provisional)
m1_interests.recalibration: pilot, with k-fold cross-validation so the same students are not used to fit and to evaluate

m2_abilities.model: Rasch (1PL) per family; 2PL only if n >= 300 for the family and item fit favours it

congruence.formula: fit = w_interest * interest_match + w_ability * ability_support + w_marks * marks_support, interest_match = (pearson_r(student_riasec_shifted, path_riasec) + 1) / 2

definitions.student_riasec_shifted: theta_plus_k = Phi(theta_k), the standard normal CDF of each interest score, so every value is in (0, 1) and order is kept
definitions.path_riasec: the path's RIASEC profile in streams.json, values in [0, 1]: the mean O*NET 31.0 Occupational Interest profile of the occupations the path leads to, rescaled (score - 1) / 6 (tools/onet_profiles.py; occupations in path_occupations.json)
definitions.ability_support: sum over the families listed for the path of alpha_k * Phi(theta_ability_k); alpha_k equal and summing to 1; unmeasured families are dropped and the rest renormalised
definitions.marks_support: mean of the path's relevant subject percentages / 100; absent marks -> term dropped and weights renormalised
definitions.range: every term is in [0, 1], so fit is in [0, 1]
definitions.sensitivity_check: report how often the top-3 changes if correlation is replaced by cosine
definitions.interest_match: Pearson correlation of the two profiles mapped to [0, 1]. Correlation compares profile shape (which types are high and low), not level. Changed from cosine on 12 Nov 2026: cosine of all-positive profiles favoured paths with flat profiles and ranked undecided students with false confidence
definitions.differentiation: Holland's differentiation: highest minus lowest of the six Phi-scaled interest scores. Below min_differentiation the interest term is dropped and the result says 'no clear interest pattern yet' (FR-51)

min_differentiation.status: provisional; calibrated in the V1 simulation on the reference sample

m3_recommender.promotion_rule: learned ranker replaces congruence only if NDCG@3 improves by >= .05 with CI excluding 0 and fairness checks pass
m3_recommender.tie_break: Work values are not part of the fit score. If two paths' fit differs by less than 0.02, they are ordered by value match (share of the path's top O*NET work values that are among the student's top 2); otherwise by interest fit. A tie-break never moves a path by more than one place.

confidence.high: all interest SE <= .35 and coverage 100% and top-1 vs top-4 margin >= delta
confidence.delta: set on the pilot: the smallest margin at which the top-1 path stays top-1 in >= 90% of 200 bootstrap resamples of the student's own choices; bands describe stability, never probabilities

letter_reveal.note: SE starts near 1.0 (the prior), so the letter starts unreadable; it is fully readable at mean SE <= 0.35, the same SE as the High-confidence rule

fairness.primary_metric: difference in STEM top-1 rate between gender groups at matched interest and ability scores (logistic regression), with a 95% CI

quality.effect: lowers confidence and may suggest one more week; never blocks or shames
